headline: Sell the Swiss franc: buy USDCHF on a dip to VWAP and GBPCHF for the week, and keep a risk-off US100 short.
market_summary: The dollar is the strongest currency (DXY 4H RSI 76.9, daily uptrend) and the franc is turning lower on the Daily RRG while speculators sit at a record-crowded CHF long (COT Composite 100). Risk tone is defensive: VIX 24, US and European indices oversold on the 4H with US30/US500 week z near -1.1 to -1.3. Rate spreads back the CHF-funded longs (USD 2y 4.82% and GBP 2y 4.99% vs CHF 0.29%). Many oversold pairs carry bullish divergences, so the desk avoids chasing USD strength against EUR and GBP into the week's lows.

horizon_view.1d: Breakout above the 20-bar high 0.84358 is fresh but Stoch 84.6 is overbought - buy the pullback to session VWAP 0.8417; 1d target near 0.8470 (about 0.7 sigma).
horizon_view.3d: Best horizon: Daily RRG Leading, daily uptrend and a widening USD-CHF 2y spread give room for ~90 pips (0.7 of the 3-day sigma of 127).
horizon_view.5d: Trend can extend to 0.8530 if the CHF crowd starts to unwind; CHF fat tails (very high kurtosis) mean gaps are possible.

ideas.thesis: The one idea all four analysts back. USD is the strongest currency, CHF is losing momentum fastest on the Daily RRG, and speculators are at a maximum CHF long that historically unwinds. Enter on a pullback rather than at the breakout.
evidence: Tech: 4H closed above the 20-bar high 0.84358 breakout; price > SMA20 (+1.35 ATR) > SMA200 (+6.84 ATR); daily trend up, daily RSI 67.1.
COT: CHF Composite 100, NC %K52 98, NC long ratio at its 52-week max - an extreme crowd that is contrarian-bearish for CHF.
Flow: USDCHF Daily RRG Leading (101.85 / 101.44); CHF Daily RS-Momentum 97.76, the sharpest drop on the board; week z only +0.25, not stretched.
Macro: USD 2y 4.817% vs CHF 0.289%, spread 4.53% and widening (+4.5 bp in 1w, +46 bp in 13w).
risks: Developing bearish RSI/MACD/Stoch divergences and weekly VWAP z +1.88 - a deeper pullback before the move.
A risk-off spike can bid CHF as a haven, and CHF series have extreme tail risk.
The limit at 0.8417 may not fill if USD keeps running.
event_risk: Thu 20:30 BKK USD jobless claims / Philly Fed

horizon_view.1d: Bear stack and MACD histogram -8.3; first target 26960 (about 0.6 of the 1-day sigma of 458 points).
horizon_view.3d: Best horizon: retest of the week and 20-bar low 26606 while speculators keep trimming longs.
horizon_view.5d: Extension toward the 60-bar low 26273 if risk-off persists (VIX 24).

ideas.thesis: A separate, risk-off theme that every analyst voted for. The Nasdaq is below both moving averages with negative momentum, speculators are cutting longs from a near-extreme, and US data has been soft. Unlike US30, it is not yet statistically stretched.
evidence: Tech: price < SMA20 (27477) < SMA200 (29190); MACD histogram -8.3; RSI 43.0 leaves room to fall.
COT: Nasdaq-100 NC %K52 fell from 89 to 82 with a -13,742 weekly change - specs unwinding from a near-extreme.
Flow: week z -0.95 (US30 is already -1.32), so US100 is the index with the most room left.
Macro: soft US data (industrial production -0.4%, building permits 1.295M vs 1.377M) and VIX 22.9-24.
risks: US500/US30 are close to oversold and Tech flags bounce risk across indices.
A tech-led relief rally or a positive headline can squeeze shorts quickly.
COT is a week old; the next report is due Friday.

ideas.invalidation: 4H close above 27600 (back above SMA20 and the previous-day high 27445).

horizon_view.1d: Capped by the 20/60-bar high 1.11159; UK retail sales Friday 14:00 can whip the entry - a small 1d target only.
horizon_view.3d: A break of 1.1116 opens 1.1190 (about 0.6 of the 3-day sigma of 172).
horizon_view.5d: Best horizon: BoE-hike carry plus the crowded CHF long unwinding; 1.1230 is about 0.6 of the 5-day sigma.

ideas.thesis: The highest-carry currency against the most crowded funding currency. GBP speculator positioning jumped after the BoE hike while CHF sits at a bullish extreme, and the pair leads on the Daily RRG. It is the second CHF-short idea on the desk, so the two share the franc risk.
evidence: COT: GBP Composite jumped from 45 to 76 (NC +16,605 on the week); CHF Composite 100, CM %K52 5.
Flow: GBPCHF Daily RRG Leading (102.34 / 102.53, dy +1.09); CHF Daily Weakening; retail positioning balanced.
Macro: GBP 2y 4.989% (BoE hiked to 4.00%) vs CHF 0.289%, spread 4.70%, +6.4 bp in 1w.
Tech: 4H price > SMA20 (1.10837) > SMA200 (1.1019); no strong 4H trigger yet (neutral vote).
risks: Shares the CHF leg with idea #1 - together they are one larger CHF short.
GBP is Lagging on the 4H RRG and heading down-left; UK retail sales Friday is inside the 1-day window.
Extreme kurtosis in CHF crosses - stops can gap.

also_considered.why_not: Tech, Flow and Macro were for it, but COT showed EUR speculators at a bearish extreme that is starting to cover (Composite 0 to 6, +21,395 on the week), and several bullish 4H divergences sit at the week low.
Only Tech was for it; MACD just crossed up and the other analysts were neutral.
COT was against it: the JPY speculator long is still building and NZD positioning is turning up from an extreme; JPY CPI on Friday.
Contrarian bounce idea (retail 25% long, RSI 28) with Flow and Macro for it, but it fights the 20-bar breakdown and the desk's risk-off call.

dissent: Tech wanted to stay with JPY-cross shorts (NZDJPY, GBPJPY) while COT argued the JPY long is too crowded; Flow and Macro wanted EURUSD short, which COT vetoed because EUR shorts are already at an extreme.
